hypotheses.justification: It is an instance-implicit section variable (declared at `variable [OpensMeasurableSpace E] [SecondCountableTopology E]`, line 913), so Lean includes it as an argument of the theorem, but nothing in the statement or in the argument needs it. The statement only uses `[MeasurableSpace E]` (to form `Measure (E × E)`) and the integrand `‖z.1 - z.2‖ ^ 2 = ‖(z.1 - z.2)‖ ^ 2` is measurable purely from `[OpensMeasurableSpace E]` (continuity of subtraction on `E × E` together with `MeasurableSpace (E × E)` and continuity of the norm); no separability is involved. In the proof, `[SecondCountableTopology E]` is only passed along to `TauCeti.memLp_of_hasFiniteMoment_map` (line 924) and `TauCeti.HasFiniteMoment.memLp_id` (line 917), which carry it only because the same `variable` is in scope: `memLp_id` is proved from `memLp_congr_enorm` and `HasFiniteMoment.memLp`, the latter living in the earlier `MetricMoment` section with hypothesis `[PseudoMetricSpace X]` and proved from `memLp_edist_iff_of_edist_ne_top` (`memLp_const_enorm`, `MemLp.add`, `MemLp.of_le_enorm`), and `memLp_of_hasFiniteMoment_map` is proved from `memLp_map_measure_iff`; none of these lemmas assumes a second-countable topology. Hence adding `omit [SecondCountableTopology E] in` to those two auxiliary lemmas makes the very same proof compile with the argument deleted, so the result is still provable without it. The remaining arguments cannot be deleted: `[IsFiniteMeasure π]` is essential because the basepoint change in `memLp_edist_iff_of_edist_ne_top`/`HasFiniteMoment.memLp` needs finiteness (for `π = ∞ • δ_{(0,1)}` on `ℝ × ℝ` both marginals have finite second moment at their atoms, while `∫⁻ ‖z.1 - z.2‖² ∂π = ∞`); `h₁` (resp. `h₂`) is essential (e.g. `λ ⊗ δ_0` with `λ` a probability measure on `ℝ` of infinite second moment); and `[OpensMeasurableSpace E]` is essential (with `MeasurableSpace E = ⊥`, `π = δ_{(0,0)}` satisfies `h₁`, `h₂`, yet `‖z.1 - z.2‖ ^ 2` is not a.e. strongly measurable, so it is not `Integrable`).
